title: Making a marble run
examples: Teacher, what is the best angle for the slide?
If I make the track wider, will it go faster?
How do I make the marble turn without stopping?

explain.say: Today we are building a cool marble run.
First we need to think about slopes for gravity to pull it.
A steeper slope means the marble will go much faster.
Next we need to plan the turns so the marble stays on track.
We must always test our run and fix what is not working.
In real life, water slides use these same ideas.

draw.text: Water slides use slopes and turns

faq.q: Does the angle of the slope matter more than the length?
faq.a: Yes, a steeper slope will make the marble go faster even if the run is shorter. You can also ask if the angle is more important than the length.
asks: Is steepness more important than distance?
Which makes it go faster, angle or length?

faq.q: What is the best kind of turn to use?
faq.a: A gentle curve is best because it keeps the marble moving smoothly. You might also ask what kind of turn is easiest.
asks: Should the turn be sharp or round?
How do I make a smooth corner?

faq.q: If it stops, should I just add more slope?
faq.a: Sometimes adding more slope helps, but you should also check if the turn is too tight. You could also ask what else to check.
asks: Does it stop because of the turn?

faq.q: Do I need to use the same material for everything?
faq.a: No, you can use different materials for different parts. This lets you test how different things work together. You might also ask about mixing materials.
asks: Can I use cardboard and plastic?

faq.q: How do I make it go further?
faq.a: Try making the slope steeper or adding more length to the track. You can also check if the turns are too sharp.
asks: What makes the marble travel farther?
How do I increase the distance?

facts: Gravity pulls the marble down the slope.
A steeper slope increases the marble's speed.
Gentle curves help the marble maintain momentum.
Testing and fixing is part of engineering.

quiz.say: If you want the marble to move quickly, should you use a very shallow slope or a very steep slope?
quiz.why: A steep slope uses gravity's pull to make the marble move very fast.

wrong.0: A medium slope is okay, but it is not as fast as a steep one.
wrong.1: No slope means no pull from gravity, so it will not move.
wrong.3: A shallow slope makes the marble move slowly because gravity pulls less.

quiz.say: When designing the turns, what shape is best for the marble?
quiz.why: A gentle curve keeps the marble moving smoothly without losing too much speed.

wrong.0: A straight line is good, but it does not help with turning.
wrong.1: Loops are hard to build and can sometimes stop the marble.
wrong.3: A sharp corner makes the marble lose energy and might fall off.

quiz.say: If the marble falls off the track, what should you do next?
quiz.why: Falling off means the design needs checking, so you must test and then fix it.

wrong.0: Making it bigger does not fix the weak spot that caused the fall.
wrong.2: Starting over is too much work; you should only fix the problem area.
wrong.3: Ignoring the problem means the marble will keep falling off.
